NDT training in Evansville, IN: how it works

Short answer: Evansville-area technicians learn NDT theory online on the Atlantis portal at whatever pace their shifts allow, ask an ASNT NDT Level III when something is unclear, and finish with a hands-on practical at their employer's own plant under a written practice based on ASNT SNT-TC-1A. Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Evansville. Courses run at Level 1, 2 and 3 in UT, RT, MT, PT and VT, access starts the moment you enroll, and we reply within one business day.

Evansville anchors the Tri-State, the stretch of the Ohio River valley where southwest Indiana, western Kentucky and southeastern Illinois meet. Heavy industry lines the river on both sides. Downstream in Posey County, CountryMark runs a crude oil refinery at Mount Vernon, and a large plastics plant operated by SABIC sits nearby. Upstream in Warrick County, Alcoa operates an aluminum smelter near Newburgh, alongside the Warrick rolling mill that Kaiser Aluminum bought from Alcoa. North of the city, Toyota assembles vehicles at its Indiana plant in Princeton. Coal and gas-fired generating stations, barge and towboat operators and river terminals complete the picture.

Across the bridges, Henderson County in Kentucky adds Century Aluminum's Sebree smelter and its own share of manufacturing and power work, and many technicians who live in Evansville clock in on the Kentucky side. For training purposes the river matters less than the work: a refinery inspector, a smelter maintenance technician and a fabrication-shop examiner all need the same SNT-TC-1A grounding, then the codes and acceptance criteria of the employer they work for.

To talk through your own situation, ask about NDT training in Evansville and say which method, level and employer you have in mind.

How to get NDT certified in Evansville: the SNT-TC-1A path step by step

Neither Indiana nor Kentucky licenses NDT technicians. Instead, each employer adopts a written practice based on ASNT SNT-TC-1A and certifies its own staff against it, method by method and level by level. Completing a course gives you documented training hours; the employer's signature is what certifies you.

  1. Confirm the requirements. Run your details through the SNT-TC-1A eligibility checker to see the training and experience hours for your target method and level.
  2. Read the employer's written practice. It defines your hours, examination content, vision checks and recertification interval. Contractors serving the refinery or the smelters may also have to satisfy the site owner's contractor rules.
  3. Finish the formal training. Complete the self-paced theory on the Atlantis portal and send questions to the Level III as you work. SNT-TC-1A recommended hours for each method appear in the training-requirements matrix.
  4. Log supervised experience. Record time performing the method on real work under a certified Level II or Level III. Experience nearly always takes longer to accumulate than coursework.
  5. Clear the vision examination. Near vision and color contrast are tested at the interval in your written practice.
  6. Pass the written examinations. The general examination covers method principles; the specific examination covers your employer's procedures, equipment and acceptance standards.
  7. Pass the practical examination. You test real specimens with your employer's equipment under Level III oversight.
  8. Get certified. The employer signs the certification and keeps the file ready for customer and owner audits.
  9. Recertify on time. SNT-TC-1A recommends a maximum interval of five years, and many written practices set a shorter one.

If you change employers often, consider ASNT central certification as well: ASNT 9712 for Level I and II, or the ASNT NDT Level III examinations. Atlantis prepares candidates for both. The NDT training FAQ covers the questions people ask most.

Level 1, Level 2 and Level 3 NDT courses for Evansville technicians

Courses follow the SNT-TC-1A body of knowledge for each method, and an ASNT NDT Level III teaches them. They get you ready for your employer's examinations rather than certifying you directly.

MethodWhat the course coversWhere it is used around Evansville
VT (visual)Viewing conditions, measuring tools, weld and corrosion features, documentationRefinery piping walk-downs, structural steel, barge and terminal repairs, final weld checks
MT (magnetic particle)Yoke and prod techniques, field direction, particle selection, interpreting and recording indicationsSteel welds on equipment and structures, crane components, shafts and couplings at plants along the river
PT (penetrant)Pre-cleaning, penetrant and developer systems, dwell control, evaluationAluminum parts and welds at the smelter and rolling mill, stainless process piping, non-magnetic castings
UT (ultrasonic)Wave physics, instrument calibration, thickness gauging, straight-beam and angle-beam weld examinationCorrosion monitoring on refinery and power-plant piping, tank and vessel shells, heavy plate and welds
RT (radiographic)Exposure planning, image quality, film and digital interpretation, radiation safety principlesPipe welds on new construction and repairs, castings and pressure-boundary work where specified
Level III preparationASNT Basic and Method examination preparation, written practice and procedure developmentEmployers and contractors that need a responsible Level III for their program

Most newcomers start with Level 1 training and move to Level 2 training once their experience log supports it. Senior Level IIs preparing to run a program can begin ASNT Level III preparation.

Ultrasonic testing (UT) training in Evansville

Ultrasonic thickness gauging is probably the single most common NDT task in the Evansville region. Refineries, chemical plants, power stations and river terminals all carry piping, tanks and vessels that thin over time from corrosion and erosion, and owners need dependable readings at fixed monitoring locations to decide what to repair during the next outage. A technician who can calibrate correctly, read through coatings with the right technique and report trends clearly is useful at almost every plant on the river.

Angle-beam weld examination is the next skill up. New piping, structural steel and fabricated equipment for these plants call for volumetric examination of welds, and UT handles much of it. The course covers sound propagation, transducers and wedges, reference blocks, distance-amplitude correction, scanning patterns and flaw sizing, then the practical on your employer's equipment turns those ideas into habits.

Visual and magnetic particle work still come first for most beginners, and penetrant is unusually important here because of the aluminum industry, where MT cannot be used on the metal itself. Check your UT theory with the UT Level 2 practice questions, and see the full outline on the ultrasonic testing training page.

Where NDT technicians work around Evansville

Refining and chemicals. CountryMark's Mount Vernon refinery processes crude oil into fuels, and the plastics plant at Mount Vernon runs large process units of its own. Pressure equipment in these plants is inspected to API in-service codes and repaired to ASME standards, with contract crews swelling during turnarounds. Atlantis does not train for API inspector certifications; some refinery roles ask for one in addition to NDT method certification.

Aluminum. The Warrick smelter and rolling mill near Newburgh, and the Sebree smelter in Henderson County, Kentucky, run pot lines, casthouses, rolling stands, cranes and large power and utility systems. Maintenance inspection covers welds, crane structures, rotating equipment and heavy aluminum and steel components, with penetrant and ultrasonic methods prominent.

Automotive. Toyota's assembly plant in Princeton and its supplier base in southwest Indiana inspect stamped, welded and cast parts to customer quality requirements, and plant maintenance teams look after presses, conveyors and robots.

Power generation. Coal and gas-fired stations along the Ohio River in Indiana and Kentucky carry boilers, high-energy piping and turbines that are inspected during planned outages, usually under ASME boiler and piping codes and the owner's own program.

River industry and fabrication. Barge builders, towboat repair yards, grain and coal terminals and structural fabricators weld steel to AWS, U.S. Coast Guard and classification-society requirements, generating steady VT, MT and UT work. Where welding inspection sits beside NDT, the six-day AWS CWI exam-prep course is an option; AWS administers the exam and issues the certification.

Public pay data for these roles is summarized in the NDT salary guide; local offers vary with method, level, travel and turnaround overtime.

NDT schools and classes near Evansville: what to compare

When people in the Tri-State look for NDT classes, they usually find either a classroom-based school some distance away or a self-paced program with the practical done at an employer's facility. A school with its own equipment suits someone with no NDT employer who wants bench time before job hunting. Self-paced theory plus an employer-site practical suits technicians already on a payroll and companies that cannot release staff for weeks of travel.

Ivy Tech Community College has an Evansville campus and offers welding certificates and AWS certification preparation through its Indiana campuses. That is a sensible base for anyone heading toward weld inspection, though welding training is not NDT method certification. Put these questions to any NDT provider before you sign up:

  • Which methods and levels are covered, and are the training hours documented against SNT-TC-1A?
  • Does the instructor hold ASNT NDT Level III in that method?
  • How and where will you get hands-on practice, and on what kind of specimens?
  • Will your current or future employer's written practice accept the training records?
  • Is preparation for ASNT central certification included if you want it?
  • What does the published fee cover, and what comes on top?

Online NDT training in Indiana and Kentucky

Turnaround seasons, rotating shifts and long drives across the river make fixed class times hard to keep in the Tri-State. Online theory avoids that problem. The Atlantis portal holds the Level 1 and Level 2 material for each method plus Level III preparation, you study when your schedule allows, and an ASNT NDT Level III answers questions as they come up. Access begins the moment you enroll, and courses run year-round.

Online study covers theory only; the practical and its examination are done in person at your employer's facility, with the Practical NDT simulator for rehearsal. Statewide pages cover NDT training in Indiana and NDT training in Kentucky, and NDT training in the USA sets out the national options alongside the full training catalog. The published US fees for standard courses are in the table on this page, and Register & Buy Now opens the course on the Atlantis portal.

Training a crew at your Evansville facility

Plants and contractors in Vanderburgh, Warrick, Posey and Gibson counties, and on the Kentucky side, often need several technicians qualified before an outage or a new contract. The practical approach is to enroll the group in self-paced theory, let them log experience on live work, and then complete the hands-on training and examinations at your site with your instruments and representative parts.

  • Program check: make sure your written practice reflects every method and technique your crew performs; written practice development helps when it does not.
  • Study phase: theory online, questions to the Level III, simulator rehearsal between shifts.
  • Site phase: an ASNT NDT Level III delivers the hands-on practical and examinations in person under your written practice.
  • Records: you certify and file; outside Level III consulting can support procedures, audits and owner reviews.

Plan around outage windows and contract start dates. Send your crew size and methods and we reply within one business day.

Radiography licensing in Indiana and Kentucky

An RT course teaches exposure technique and film or digital interpretation, but it does not license anybody to use radiation sources. The two sides of the river are regulated differently. On the Indiana side, as of September 30, 2026, Indiana is an NRC Agreement State, so its own radioactive materials program, rather than the Nuclear Regulatory Commission, now licenses industrial radiography with radioactive sources under rules compatible with 10 CFR Part 34. Kentucky is an Agreement State, and its Cabinet for Health and Family Services licenses radioactive materials in Kentucky. A radiography company working on both sides needs authorization in each jurisdiction, through its own license or reciprocity, and its radiographers must meet the radiation safety training and certification rules that apply. Atlantis does not perform radiography in the US.

Practice before your practical exam

Rehearsal shortens the gap between reading and doing. The Practical NDT simulator runs in a browser and covers 12 method families across 12 workplaces, including a storage tank and an oil and gas site, so refinery and terminal trainees can practice setups that resemble their own work. The free NDT practice tests cover the written side. Both help you find weak areas early; neither stands in for experience hours or the practical examination on real specimens.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Evansville

How do I become an NDT technician in Evansville?

Complete Level 1 training in a method such as VT, MT or UT, find an employer with an SNT-TC-1A written practice, log supervised experience, and pass the vision, written and practical examinations. Your employer then certifies you.

What does NDT training cost in Evansville?

Look at the published US fees in the table on this page for the standard courses. Crew training at your site and Level III services are quoted on request, and we reply within one business day.

Can I study NDT online if I work shifts at a plant?

Yes. Theory is self-paced on the Atlantis portal, so you can fit it around rotating shifts and turnarounds. Hands-on practice and the practical examination take place in person at your employer's facility.

Is there NDT training near me in Evansville?

Atlantis does not operate a school in the Tri-State. The theory is online, and practical training and examinations happen at the employer's own facility, which for working technicians often means no travel at all.

Which method is most useful for Evansville jobs?

UT thickness gauging is in constant demand at refineries, power plants and terminals. Start with VT and MT, add PT for the aluminum industry, then build UT skills as your experience grows.

I live in Evansville but work in Kentucky. Does that change anything?

Not for NDT method certification, which follows your employer's written practice in either state. It does matter for radiography, because Kentucky and Indiana handle radiation licensing differently.

Will my certification follow me to another employer?

No. Each employer certifies under its own written practice, so a new employer reviews your records and may ask for fresh examinations. ASNT central certification is the more portable option.

Do you teach API 510, 570 or 653?

No. Atlantis focuses on SNT-TC-1A method training, Level III preparation and a six-day AWS CWI exam-prep course. API inspector certification is handled through API's own program.
